chapter: Chicago friends: Tesch, Stacy and Wettling
title: Stacy and Cliff Leeman's duet date and Carnegie Hall ovation
summary: A piano-drums duet session led to Stacy playing Carnegie Hall and getting a standing ovation, while Freeman was still with the World's Greatest Jazz Band.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: Yes, just on the publicity he's gotten, you know, making a comeback and of course, the New Yorker article, which is a tremendous piece. That is big international stuff, I think he would get the greatest surprise of his life, because when we played in the trio, we played -- we did a duet date since we were recording a duet, we had Cliff Leeman on drums and Jess and Cliff didn't hit -- they didn't get on too well together, so we decided without offending Cliff, who is a super drummer, that we would do a session with just piano and drums -- and George Wean heard about this and so he put us on to Carnegie Hall and we played two num-

bers, we played Don't Blame Me as a ballad and some blues in F in a fast tempo, and I couldn't -- Jess got a standing ovation and I couldn't get him to stand up, he was so scared, but he played beautifully.
From that time on, Jess Stacy could do no wrong, He was now becoming an idol--
What year was that, do you remember?
Well, as I said, I think we did the concert -- I had been over here three and a half years, so that must have been four or five years ago.
Well, I have been over three and a half, so let's say it's a little over four years.
Because I was still with the World's Greatest Jazz Band, and we came back here -- You see, I left the World's Greatest Jazz Band here.
